Confirmed: in `guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java`, `Segment.get()` (lines 2065/2102) calls `recordRead(e, now)` (defined at lines 2542-2547) without holding the segment lock; it simply appends the entry to the `recencyQueue` field (line 1948). That queue is later drained — under the segment lock (`@GuardedBy("this")`) — by `Segment.drainRecencyQueue()` (lines 2590-2602), which pops entries and moves them to the proper position in the LRU access queue.

ANSWER: On a read, `Segment.get()` calls `recordRead(entry, now)` (guava/src/com/google/common/cache/LocalCache.java:2542-2547), which lock-free appends the entry to the `recencyQueue` (a `ConcurrentLinkedQueue`, field at line 1948) instead of touching the access list directly; that queue is later drained, under the segment lock, by `Segment.drainRecencyQueue()` (lines 2590-2602), which reorders the real LRU access queue accordingly.
